notes: Rossendale has no selective or additional HMO licensing scheme. Only mandatory HMO licensing applies, for homes let to 5 or more people from 2 or more households. A new licence costs £719.70 plus £279.50 on grant. The Article 4 Direction is planning control, not licensing.
research: SITEMAP SWEEP: 72,210 URLs from sitemap.xml, grepped case-insensitively: ZERO containing 'selective'. SITE SEARCH CONTROL: PASSED and discriminating. /site-search/results/?q= returned 'occupation' 14 results, 'hmo' 14 results, 'licensing' 1360 results, and 'selective' ZERO results. The search indexes Information, Downloads and Councillors areas. FEE TEST: only mandatory HMO fees exist, quoted verbatim: 'The cost of a new HMO application is currently Part A £719.70 which needs to be paid on application. If the licence is issued then Part B charge of £279.50 is payable' and 'The cost of a renewal, after 5 years, is Part A £700.70 and Part B £279.50'. No selective or additional licence fee anywhere. LICENSING SECTION: the licensing index lists only 'Animal licences' and 'Premises Licence', no property licensing at all. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) ARTICLE 4 DIRECTION: the HMO page says 'Please ensure you apply for planning permission in the first instance see Article 4 Directions | Planning | Rossendale Borough Council'. Planning control over C3-to-C4 conversion, not licensing. (2) NEIGHBOUR BLEED: Rossendale sits in East Lancashire beside Burnley, Blackburn with Darwen and Pendle, which have run selective licensing. No Rossendale page describes a neighbour's scheme; the sitemap and search sweeps returned zero 'selective' anywhere, so there was nothing to misattribute. LIMITATION: the 'Urgent Cabinet Decision - amended wording of Private Sector Housing Renewal Strategy and Policy' PDF is a scanned image with no extractable text layer (pdftotext yielded 2 characters), so it could not be read. It is a minor amendment-of-wording item, and the council's working site search separately indexes Downloads and returned zero hits for 'selective'. ModernGov returned HTTP 522 (origin down) on repeated attempts, so committee papers were not directly reachable.

notes: Rugby has no selective or additional HMO licensing scheme. Only mandatory HMO licensing applies, for homes let to 5 or more people from 2 or more households, costing £1,362 to £1,694. The 2024 Article 4 Direction for central wards is planning control, not licensing.
research: SITEMAP SWEEP: sitemap.xml is an index of 137 sub-sitemaps; all followed, 1,008 unique URLs collected. ZERO containing 'selective'. SITE SEARCH CONTROL: PASSED. Nonsense queries 'zzzqqxywvv' and 'bananaquux' both returned 'No results', proving the engine discriminates. 'selective' returned 82 results, so each was inspected rather than accepting the count: every one is an unrelated sense of the word, being Rugby Art Gallery exhibition items ('Rugby Open', 'rising stars of contemporary art', 'Wardill returns home for the Rugby Collection'), 'tender opportunities and guidance' (selective tendering), local land charges, local plan evidence base, play rangers, public space CCTV and a tenant newsletter. /w/local-land-charges and /w/health-and-safety-in-private-rented-accommodation were fetched and grepped: ZERO occurrences of 'selective' or any housing-licensing designation. FEE TEST: mandatory only, quoted verbatim: 'The following fees* (all VAT exempt) apply to licence applications received before occupation of the HMO: £1,362 (for one to six occupants); £1,556 (for seven to 11 occupants); £1,694 (for 12+ occupants)'; 'We charge £1,177 for the renewal of an HMO licence'; 'We apply a £900 surcharge to licence applications from landlords found to be running an unlicensed HMO'. No selective or s.56 fee line. THRESHOLD: 'From 1 April 2018, if you rent out a property to five or more tenants in two or more households, you must apply for an HMO licence. The new legislation has removed the requirement for a property to have three or more storeys'. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) ARTICLE 4 DIRECTION, the biggest trap here, and Rugby has TWO pages for it. /w/article-4-direction-hmos states 'On Wednesday 25 September 2024, the council confirmed an Article 4 Direction which was made and consulted on in February 2024. The direction requires all proposed changes of use from a dwelling house (class C3) to a small HMO (class C4) to apply for planning permission, within the area defined by the direction', covering 'specifically the following wards: Benn, Coton and Boughton, Eastlands, New Bilton, Newbold and Brownsover'. A confirmed direction with a commencement date and a named ward list, which reads exactly like a designation, but it is PLANNING control and creates no licence requirement. Deliberately NOT carried into the schemes array or a ward list. (2) '/w/hmo-licence-additional-information-pack': the word 'additional' qualifies an information pack. (3) NEIGHBOUR BLEED: Coventry City (adjacent) has an additional HMO licensing scheme; no Rugby page describes it. LIMITATION: rugby.moderngov.co.uk returned HTTP 522 and democracy.rugby.gov.uk did not resolve, so committee papers were not reachable; the negative rests on the full sitemap sweep, a control-passing site search whose hits were individually inspected, and the fee schedule.

notes: Runnymede states it operates no additional or selective licensing schemes. Only mandatory HMO licensing applies, for homes let to 5 or more people from 2 or more households. The basic licence fee is £815 per licence, or £723 to renew.
research: EXPLICIT COUNCIL DENIAL, the gold standard, verified by direct fetch. The HMO page states verbatim: 'The scope of mandatory licensing has been extended to cover certain HMOs, including flats, occupied by five or more persons in two or more households, regardless of the number of storeys' followed by 'No additional or selective licensing schemes are currently in operation.' Corroborated in the council's landlord guide (updated June 2023): 'We do not currently operate any additional or selective licensing schemes.' Further corroborated by the HMO renewal factsheet issued 1 April 2026, headed 'HOUSING ACT 2004 - PART 2, LICENSING OF HOUSES IN MULTIPLE OCCUPATION', containing no Part 3 content. FEE TEST: mandatory only, quoted verbatim: 'The basic fee is £815 per licence'; 'If the managing agent is different to the licence holder, then an additional £93 applies'; 'If you need assistance with your application, or you submit an incomplete application which causes us extra time to process, the total fee is £1027 per licence'; renewal 'The basic fee is £723 per licence'. SITEMAP SWEEP: 978 URLs, ZERO containing 'selective', independently reproduced with an identical count. SITE SEARCH CONTROL: PASSED, 'council tax' returned about 3,980 results; exact-phrase 'selective licensing' returned 4 hits, all excluded below. COMMITTEE PAPERS: ModernGov control 'houses in multiple occupation' returned 7 results, and 'selective licensing' returned 'No results found' across all agendas, minutes and reports. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) CIVIL-PENALTY BOILERPLATE: the Private Sector Housing Enforcement Policy effective 1 May 2026 lists 'Offences in relation to the Selective Licensing of houses [s95 Housing Act 2004]'. (2) NATIONAL MODEL-FORM WORDING: a page heading 'HMO and Selective Licensing' introduces 'These regulations add the following mandatory conditions to selective and HMO licences', verbatim national wording about the Electrical Safety Standards in the Private Rented Sector (England) Regulations 2020 applying generically to both licence types. (3) The '£93 additional' managing-agent surcharge on a mandatory licence, not s.56. (4) s.254 DEFINITION: the landing page says 'If you have three or more unrelated tenants in one property... this is known as a house in multiple occupation'; the next page sets licensing at five. LIMITATION: none material. Note Runnymede is due to be abolished into a new Surrey unitary in April 2027; this does not affect the position today.

notes: Rushmoor has no selective or additional HMO licensing scheme. Only mandatory HMO licensing applies, for homes let to 5 or more people from 2 or more households. Fees run from £1,108 for 5 occupants to £2,214 for 21 or more, for a five-year licence.
research: SITEMAP: /sitemap.xml, /sitemap_index.xml, /sitemap-index.xml, /wp-sitemap.xml and /robots.txt ALL return 404. The working path is the bare /sitemap, from which 1,064 URLs were collected and grepped: ZERO containing 'selective'. Only three HMO URLs exist. GREP GOTCHA WORTH RECORDING: the string 'rushmoor' contains the substring 'hmo', so a naive case-insensitive grep for 'hmo' matches nearly every URL on this domain; the token 'rushmoor' must be stripped before matching. THRESHOLD: the HMO page states 'All properties that are let to five or more people, living as two or more households, must be licensed', the only licensing trigger stated, and contains zero occurrences of 'selective' or 'additional licensing'. ADOPTED POLICY: the Licensing policy for houses in multiple occupation (September 2025, 18 pages) states 'The council's HMO Licensing Policy was adopted on 6 April 2006 and introduced the national mandatory licensing scheme for large, high-risk HMOs under Part 2 of the Housing Act 2004' and 'The fees were calculated in accordance with the requirements of the Housing Act 2004 - Part 2 - Section 63 (7)'. A regex scan of the full 31,076 extracted characters returned ZERO hits for 'selective', 'additional licen', 'section 56' or 'designat'. FEE TEST: mandatory only, quoted verbatim: 'Number of people living in property / Fee for a five-year property licence: 5 - £1,108; 6 to 10 - £1,389; 11 to 15 - £1,659; 16 to 20 - £1,943; 21+ - £2,214'. The schedule starts at 5 occupants; a Part 3 or s.56 scheme would need its own fee line and there is none. SITE SEARCH CONTROL: PASSED, control 'houses in multiple occupation' returned 5 results; 'selective licensing' returned 0 results. COMMITTEE PAPERS: ModernGov control 'houses in multiple occupation' returned results over 2 pages; the bare word 'selective' returned 'No results found for your query selective' across the entire archive. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) an 'additional licensing' site-search returned 20 hits, all OR-match noise (exhibition of animals, breeding dogs, hiring out horses, selling animals as pets, dog and cat boarding, premises-licence variations, gambling representations). (2) ARTICLE 4 DIRECTIONS: Rushmoor has seven (Church Circle, Employment land 2017, Pinewood Park, Cargate, Wellesley, Employment land March 2022, Town and district centres). Each was checked: none is an HMO or C3-to-C4 direction; they are conservation-area, employment-land and town-centre directions. (3) ModernGov 'additional licensing' hits are all alcohol and premises Licensing Sub-Committee determinations. LIMITATION: the absent XML sitemap is the notable gap; had the bare /sitemap path also failed, this would have been marked UNVERIFIED rather than negative.

notes: Rutland has no selective or additional HMO licensing scheme, and publishes no housing licence fee at all. Only mandatory HMO licensing applies, for homes let to 5 or more people from 2 or more households. The service is run jointly with Peterborough City Council.
research: COUNCIL WORDING: the housing standards page states 'We share our housing standards service with Peterborough City Council. The housing standards team: ... implement mandatory licencing of houses in multiple occupation'. The council describes its own licensing function as mandatory HMO licensing and nothing else; its enforcement list otherwise cites only Part 1 HHSRS powers. FEE TEST, the strongest evidence here: the licence fees page is 'A list of all the licences available from the council and their fees' and was read in full. It covers alcohol rateable-value bands A to E, personal licences, TENs, animal boarding, dangerous wild animals, dog breeding, hackney carriage £218, private hire vehicle £218, HC/PH driver £133, gaming machine permit £50, lottery £40, pet shop, riding establishment, scrap metal collector £273, scrap metal site £392, skin piercing premises £250 and person £112, street trading £845/£288/£2,232 plus VAT, and zoo licence £350. There is NO HMO licence fee, no selective licence fee and no additional licence fee anywhere in it. A live Part 3 or s.56 scheme must carry its own cost-recovery fee; Rutland carries none. SITEMAP SWEEP: sitemap.xml is a Drupal index (lastmod 2026-08-05); 2,588 URLs collected, independently reproduced with an identical count, with ZERO containing 'selective', 'hmo', 'multiple occupation' or 'landlord'. The /licensing/ tree contains only alcohol-entertainment-gambling, animal, buying-selling-collecting, child employment and performance, petroleum and explosives, and taxi and private hire. CURRENT COMMITTEE POSITION: Cabinet, 11 August 2026, Report No. 77/2026 'Adoption of New Policies to Reflect the Changes Arising from the Renters' Rights Act 2025' seeks approval for 'a new Civil Penalties Policy, Housing Standards Enforcement Policy, and Mandatory House in Multiple Occupation (HMO) Licence conditions'. Appendix 3 opens 'HMO licences granted under Part 2 of the Housing Act 2004'. All 11 pages of Appendix 3 and all 10 pages of the main report were extracted: ZERO hits for 'selective', 'additional licen', 'section 56' or 'designat'. Rutland is actively rewriting its whole PRS licensing framework this month and it is Part 2 mandatory only. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) CIVIL-PENALTY BOILERPLATE: Appendix 1 contains 'Failure to obtain a selective licence under section 95 of the Housing Act 2004' and a tariff table 'Failure to obtain a selective licence - section 95(1): Starting point £12,000; Statutory maximum £40,000'. A hypothetical tariff copied from MHCLG statutory guidance; Rutland has no selective licence to fail to obtain. Appendix 2 carries near-identical wording to Runnymede's, confirming a shared national template. (2) NEIGHBOUR BLEED, a live risk flagged and controlled: Rutland's housing standards service is DELIVERED BY Peterborough City Council, so any Peterborough scheme would be easy to misattribute. Rutland's verdict was sourced only from rutland.gov.uk pages and Rutland's own Cabinet papers. (3) ModernGov 'additional licensing' hits are all Planning Committee development-control reports. LIMITATION: Rutland's on-site search is JavaScript-only (Cludo) and its REST API returns HTTP 401 without the site token. The site search CONTROL TEST COULD NOT BE RUN, so it was excluded from the evidence base entirely. The negative rests on four independent primary sources: the 2,588-URL sitemap sweep, the housing standards page wording, the complete licence-fee schedule containing no housing licence, and the August 2026 Cabinet papers. The ModernGov control PASSED separately.

notes: Sevenoaks has no selective or additional HMO licensing scheme. Only mandatory HMO licensing applies, for homes let to 5 or more people from 2 or more households. A new licence costs £1,031.17 for up to five units, plus £24.40 for each extra unit.
research: SITEMAP SWEEP: 2,922 URLs, grepped for selective / licen / hmo / landlord / multiple occup / private sector hous. ZERO selective- or additional-licensing pages. The only housing-licensing URLs are the single HMO page, an HMO amenity standards PDF, and the private sector housing enforcement policy. SITE SEARCH CONTROL: PASSED, control 'council tax' returned 'Results 1 - 10 of about 3350', control 'houses in multiple occupation' returned 'Results 1 - 10 of about 391', and 'selective licensing' returned 'Sorry, no results were found'. FEE TEST: mandatory only, quoted verbatim: 'The licence fee depends upon the number of units of accommodation within the property. The HMO licence fees are: A new application for up to five units is £1,031.17 and £24.40 for each additional unit. To increase the number of HMO occupiers is £102.50.' The page routes licensability to national criteria only. COMMITTEE PAPERS: ModernGov 'selective licensing' returned 3 results, all excluded below. No designation report, no consultation report and no designation notice, ever. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) '£24.40 for each additional unit', a per-unit surcharge on a mandatory licence. (2) 2006 OPTIONS PAPER: Cabinet 13/04/2006 'HMO Licensing Charges' states 'HMO licensing consists of two parts: mandatory HMO licensing and discretionary HMO additional licensing'. A pure explainer of the statutory framework. (3) APPROVED-BUT-NEVER-DESIGNATED / ASPIRATION: the 2007-2011 Private Sector Housing Strategy says work 'can be expected to increase if, following the consultation period, the Council adopts additional licensing' and action 1.2 'Consider the implementation of a Landlords Accreditation Scheme and additional licensing'. Conditional aspiration only. The same document expressly rules Part 3 out: 'selective licensing of other residential accommodation (primarily focussed upon areas of low housing demand - and unlikely to be suitable for Sevenoaks District Council)'. Even had it been adopted, a 2007-era designation would have expired by 2012 under the five-year maximum. (4) NEIGHBOUR BLEED, THANET: the 17 June 2014 Housing and Community Safety Advisory Committee pack states 'A selective licensing scheme has been put in place for the two most deprived areas in Kent, Cliftonville West and Margate Central in Thanet'. That is THANET DISTRICT COUNCIL's scheme sitting on Sevenoaks' domain, and a domain-scoped scrape would misattribute it. (5) VOLUNTARY ACCREDITATION: 'Landlords Accreditation Scheme'. (6) STATUTORY-SCOPE BOILERPLATE: a 2018 BRE stock modelling report recites the Act's scope. (7) UNRELATED SENSE: a 2018 Housing Strategy Progress Report mentions 'option to support selective use for high demand areas', concerning housing ALLOCATIONS. (8) 'each additional licensing authority' in taxi, premises and gambling notices is national model-form wording. LIMITATION: none material; sitemap, control-passing site search, service page, fee schedule and committee system were all reachable.

schemes.areaDescription: Page Hall: named streets and house-number ranges around Page Hall Road and Hinde House Lane
Named address ranges on London Road, Abbeydale Road and Chesterfield Road plus around 35 adjoining streets

notes: Sheffield has no selective licensing in force. Two schemes have ended: Page Hall (2014 to 2019) and London Road, Abbeydale Road and Chesterfield Road (2018 to 2023). Only mandatory HMO licensing now applies, for homes let to 5 or more people from 2 or more households.
research: The research brief asserted that Sheffield almost certainly HAS live selective licensing and told the researcher not to report it negative without extraordinary evidence. The evidence is extraordinary, primary, current and unambiguous, and it points the other way. THE PRIOR WAS WRONG. This was independently re-verified by the coordinator via direct fetch with a browser user-agent. Sheffield's landing page carries the summary line 'Details about the now closed Selective Licensing scheme.' SCHEME 1, PAGE HALL: 'A Selective Licence scheme ran in Page Hall from 22 April 2014 to 21 April 2019. This scheme has now ended.' followed by 'Landlords of these properties will no longer be required to apply for a selective licence to rent them out.' The designation was defined by STREETS AND HOUSE-NUMBER RANGES, not wards: Page Hall Road (53 to 135 and 52 to 118), Hinde House Lane (31 to 125 and 34 to 102), and all properties on Hinde Street, Popple Street, Robey Street, Lloyd Street, Wade Street, Lauder Street and Willoughby Street. SCHEME 2: 'A selective licensing scheme operated in areas of London Road, Abbeydale Road and Chesterfield Road, as well as some adjoining streets, between 1 November 2018 and 31 October 2023. If you previously had a Selective Licence for your property in this scheme, there is no need for you to renew as the scheme has ended.' Under 'The following addresses no longer need a licence' it lists London Road 101-661 and 42-524, Abbeydale Road 1-781 and 2-666, Chesterfield Road 13-123 and 30, plus around 35 adjoining streets with specific house numbers. 'On 26 January 2024 a report highlighting the findings from the ... selective licensing scheme was presented to the Housing Policy Committee', a closure report confirming wind-down rather than renewal. WARD-MATCHING FLAG, IMPORTANT: BOTH designations are defined by street names and house-number ranges, NOT by wards. Coverage is recorded as 'streets' and wards is null; no ward list should ever be synthesised for Sheffield. Sheffield did undergo a ward boundary review (its current 28-ward structure took effect in 2016, between the two designations), but because neither designation is ward-based, that review cannot have broken ward matching here. FEE TEST, DECISIVE: the current Fee and Charging Structure Policy (February 2024) was downloaded and text-extracted. Section 2.1: 'This policy details Sheffield City Council's licence fees and charges made during the determination process under Part 2 of the Housing Act 2004 and applies to all HMOs requiring a licence in relation to Mandatory Licensing.' The fee table is headed 'Schedule of Fees, Charges and Discounts for HMO Mandatory Licensing', new application up to 5 bedrooms Part 1 £725 plus Part 2 £460 equals £1,185, rising to £3,890 for 50+ bedrooms; renewals £1,135 to £3,840. There is NO selective and NO additional licensing fee anywhere in the document. CURRENT SCOPE: the HMO apply page states 'You need a Houses in Multiple Occupation (HMO) licence if you own a property that is occupied by 5 or more people forming 2 or more households, regardless of the number of floors'. SITEMAP SWEEP: 2,671 URLs across both sub-sitemaps; exactly three contain 'selective' and all three are the closed-scheme pages. There is no live selective licence application route. COMMITTEE SWEEP: Sheffield's Housing Policy Committee agenda and document listings were enumerated for all 14 meetings from 31 October 2024 through 22 October 2026. ZERO occurrences of 'selective' in any of them. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) THE ADDITIONAL-LICENSING RECITAL: section 1.1 of the fee policy says Sheffield has 'a statutory duty ... to administer and enforce a licensing scheme for mandatorily licensable Houses in Multiple Occupation (HMO's) and discretionary powers to implement Additional Licensing Schemes for other HMOs'. This recites the STATUTORY POWER, not its exercise. No designation, area, date or fee accompanies it, and section 2.1 immediately confines the policy to mandatory licensing. (2) s.254 DEFINITION: the HMO information page says HMOs are 'a house or a flat in which 3 or more households live as their only or main residence'; the same page then states 'Some HMOs, occupied by 5 or more will require licensing'. (3) 'Additional fit and proper declaration form' and 'Additional compliance monitoring fee £500', where 'additional' qualifies a form and a monitoring surcharge. (4) EXPIRED SCHEMES PRESENTED AS LIVE: the page for the second scheme is still TITLED 'Apply for a Selective Licence in London, Abbeydale or Chesterfield Road', which reads as live and is precisely the trap the brief warned about; its body text confirms the scheme ended on 31 October 2023. LIMITATION: Sheffield's on-site search FAILED its control test and was not relied on: /search?search= returned the identical 'We've found 841 results' for the control 'houses in multiple occupation' and for 'selective licensing', so it does not discriminate. WebFetch received HTTP 403 from sheffield.gov.uk; that was a bot block, not evidence, and every page was retrieved successfully on retry with a browser user-agent.

notes: Shropshire has no selective or additional HMO licensing scheme. Its civil penalty policy, adopted in June 2026, is the version written for councils with no selective licensing areas. Mandatory HMO licensing costs £1,055 for up to five bedrooms, plus £403 on grant.
research: THE DECISIVE SOURCE: Shropshire's Cabinet adopted a new Civil Penalty Policy on 10 June 2026. Its title block reads verbatim: 'Civil Penalties under the Renters Rights Act 2025 and other housing legislation Policy. Policy for adoption by local authorities in England (no selective licensing areas).' Shropshire selected the model-policy variant explicitly drafted for authorities that have NO SELECTIVE LICENSING AREAS. A council-adopted, two-month-old, self-declared negative, and the strongest possible form of evidence for a nil finding. The Cabinet printed decisions confirm adoption rather than proposal: 'RESOLVED: ... To approve the Shropshire Housing Authority Enforcement Policy and Civil Penalty Policy, to take effect immediately, with transitional arrangements allowing the existing policies to operate in tandem for a six-month period to conclude legacy cases.' SITEMAP SWEEP: Shropshire has no XML sitemap (/sitemap.xml 404s), so the HTML sitemap was used: 2,218 URLs collected and grepped. The only housing-licensing hits are the HMO page, landlord responsibilities and the enforcement policy. Notably the licensing-fees tree has ten sub-pages (animal, firework, gambling, taxi, Licensing Act, miscellaneous, public health, caravan-site fit-and-proper) and NOT ONE housing-licensing fee page. FEE TEST: mandatory only, quoted verbatim: 'The licence fee is as follows from 1 April 2026: Payment one: ... £1055.00 up to and including five bedrooms, and a further £176 per each additional bedroom thereafter. Payment two: must be paid within 28 days of the date of your licence. £403.00'. Threshold is the national mandatory one: 'Nationally, HMOs occupied by five or more people, in two or more households, where there is sharing of facilities, eg kitchen or bathroom, must be licensed. This is a mandatory government requirement.' COMMITTEE PAPERS: ModernGov control PASSED. 'selective licensing' returns only the June 2026 policy plus AONB terms-of-reference and planning items using 'selective' in other senses; 'additional licensing' returns only hackney carriage and private hire items. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) CIVIL-PENALTY BOILERPLATE, the single most dangerous trap in this batch, because it sits INSIDE the very document that proves the negative. The adopted Enforcement Policy lists 'Offences in relation to the Selective Licensing of houses [s95 Housing Act 2004]', and the Civil Penalty Policy lists 'Failure to obtain a selective licence under section 95 of the Housing Act 2004' and 'Failure to comply with selective licence conditions under section 95' (verified at lines 94 and 105 of the extracted text). Read in isolation these look like proof of a scheme; the same document's title block at line 7 says the opposite. (2) 'The Housing and Planning Act 2016 extends mandatory HMO licensing to include additional HMOs of all storeys', where 'additional' qualifies HMOs, describing the October 2018 nationwide removal of the storey test. (3) '£176 per each additional bedroom', a mandatory-licence surcharge. (4) s.254 DEFINITION: 'An HMO is a house or flat that is occupied as a main residence, by more than one household'; the same page sets licensing at five or more. (5) UNRELATED SENSES: Shropshire Hills AONB Partnership terms of reference and a Former Shelton Hospital planning application; a 2019 'Proposed Additional Consultation Relating to the Hackney Carriage and Private Hire Licensing Policy' is taxi licensing. LIMITATION: Shropshire has no XML sitemap AND its on-site search FAILED its control test, being JavaScript-driven and returning byte-identical 299,633-character shells for both 'houses in multiple occupation' and 'selective licensing'. It was not relied on. The negative rests on the 2,218-URL HTML sitemap sweep, the service pages, the fee schedule and a control-passing ModernGov search.

notes: Solihull has no selective or additional HMO licensing scheme. A 2022 draft housing strategy suggested exploring selective licensing, but no scheme was ever designated. Only mandatory HMO licensing applies, costing £1,075, with a £108 discount for NRLA members.
research: SITEMAP SWEEP: 1,450 URLs, independently reproduced with an identical count, ZERO containing 'selective'. The only housing-licensing URLs are /housing/homes-multiple-occupation, /housing/renting-private-landlord and /housing/solihull-landlord-forum. SITE SEARCH CONTROL: PASSED, control 'council tax' returned 'Showing items 1 to 10 of 72 results', control 'houses in multiple occupation' returned 6 results, and 'selective licensing' returned 3 results, all irrelevant fuzzy word-matches (lists and registers, health information, Balsall Common history). FEE TEST: mandatory only, quoted verbatim: 'Homes in Multiple Occupation (HMOs) are buildings that contain five or more people, two or more of which are of different households, regardless of the storey level'; 'you will be required to pay the £1,075 non-refundable fee. There are discounts for National Residential Landlords Association (NRLA) members: NRLA discount: £108'; 'Further fees may be included depending on different aspects of your HMO: an additional let or person over 7: £43.00; application for a subsequent licence resulting from the change of the licence holder: £215; inadequate application resulting in the Council reviewing information: £145'. No selective or additional licence fee anywhere. The statutory registers page lists only hackney carriage and private hire driver registers under 'Licensing'. COMMITTEE PAPERS: ModernGov control PASSED. 'selective licensing' returns EXACTLY ONE result in the entire committee archive: Economic Development, Managed Growth and Skills Scrutiny Board, 17 November 2022, 'Draft Housing Strategy'. THE 2022 ITEM IS NOT A DESIGNATION, analysed in full. Appendix 2, page 17, verbatim: 'Selective Licensing policy - Local councils can introduce selective licensing schemes where this is supported by evidence and consultation occurs. A policy would mean that all landlords in a designated area would require a licence.' Entirely conditional and generic, naming NO area, ward, street, start date, end date or fee. Appendix 3 lists '6. Private Rented Sector - Selective Licencing' as a future 'Key Thing to Do' with a four-stage pipeline: '1. Develop evidence base and proposals 2. Agree recommendations 3. Cabinet approval and Consultation 4. Notice and Implementation'. Stages 3 and 4 would each generate a Cabinet report, a statutory consultation and a designation notice, all of which would appear in ModernGov; the archive contains NONE of them. The pipeline never advanced past stage 1. Recorded as no scheme rather than 'proposed', since the only artefact is a four-year-old conditional strategy line with no live proposal behind it. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) NEIGHBOUR BLEED, BIRMINGHAM, checked explicitly and cleared. Birmingham operates a large selective licensing scheme and Solihull borders it. Every occurrence of 'Birmingham' in the Draft Housing Strategy was inspected: all 14 relate to the Greater Birmingham and Solihull LEP, the Birmingham and Black Country Housing Market Area, the Birmingham and Solihull Integrated Care System, Birmingham Airport and University Hospitals Birmingham NHS FT. (2) ARTICLE 4 DIRECTION, present here and ADJACENT TO the licensing item, making it especially dangerous. The same Implementation Plan, item 7 (HMOs), reads 'Review the case for working to introduce Article 4 Direction (area based or borough wide)'. The phrase 'area based or borough wide' reads exactly like a designation, but this is planning control over C3-to-C4 permitted development. (3) 'an additional let or person over 7: £43.00', a mandatory-licence surcharge. (4) ModernGov 'additional licensing' hits are all taxi, gambling and premises licensing. (5) VOLUNTARY ENGAGEMENT: the landlord forum and 2025 landlord forum news items are advice and engagement events. LIMITATION: none material.

notes: Somerset has no selective or additional HMO licensing scheme, and none was inherited from the former district councils. Only mandatory HMO licensing applies, for homes let to 5 or more people from 2 or more households. A new licence costs £949 in total.
research: SITEMAP SWEEP: wp-sitemap.xml index resolving to 34 sub-sitemaps, all fetched, 5,803 URLs collected, independently reproduced with an identical count. ZERO URLs containing 'selective'. The only HMO URLs are /housing-support/hmo-licensing/, /housing-support/hmo-standards-and-regulations/ and the licensing privacy notice. THRESHOLD: the HMO licensing page, last updated 17 July 2026 and therefore current, states 'The Housing Act 2004 made it mandatory for housing in multiple occupation (HMOs) be licenced' and 'An HMO licence is required if: the property is occupied by 5 or more people, from more than one household; and they share basic amenities'. No second licensable category is described. FEE TEST: mandatory only, quoted verbatim: 'New HMO Licence (5 bed max) ... Part 1 £738 / Part 2 £211 / Total £949 / Additional person over five £43' and 'Renewal HMO Licence (5 bed max) ... Part 1 £625 / Part 2 £211 / Total £836 / Additional person over five £33'. PRIVACY NOTICE CORROBORATION: the Private Sector Housing team's licensing privacy notice is titled 'Licensing of HMOs and Caravan/Camping', so no Part 3 regime is processed. The public register is county-wide ('the full register which includes the whole of Somerset'), confirming a single unified post-2023 regime. INHERITED DISTRICT DESIGNATIONS, CHECKED AND CLEARED, the key risk for this council. Somerset is a unitary formed on 1 April 2023 from Somerset County Council plus Mendip, Sedgemoor, South Somerset and Somerset West and Taunton. A pre-April-2023 district designation could in principle still run to around 2028 under the five-year maximum. All four predecessor domains now redirect to somerset.gov.uk/we-have-moved/, so the unified site is the authoritative record. Each predecessor domain was additionally swept via the Wayback CDX archive API: ZERO archived URLs matching 'selective' on all four. No such designation ever existed. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) ARTICLE 4 DIRECTION, SOUTH SOMERSET / YEOVIL, the biggest trap here. The archived South Somerset site holds hmodirection.pdf, hmo_all_zones.pdf and five zone maps filed under /planning-and-building-control/. The parent page reads 'Houses in Multiple Occupation (HMO's) - Yeovil ... Confirmation of an Article 4 Direction ... South Somerset District Council has confirmed an Article 4 Direction which now requires a planning application to be submitted ... Direction only relates to certain areas of Yeovil ... The Direction came into force on 19th November'. Zone and ward names plus a commencement date make this read exactly like a designation, but it is planning control over C3-to-C4 conversion. (2) 'Additional person over five' fee lines (£43 and £33), per-occupant surcharges on a mandatory licence. LIMITATION: Somerset's on-site search FAILED its control test, rendering results client-side via JavaScript and returning zero result rows even for control queries, so it was not relied on. Somerset's ModernGov also failed its control test: ieSearchResults.aspx returns page chrome only via both GET and POST, so committee papers could not be keyword-searched. A designation existing ONLY in an un-indexed committee report, and not yet reflected in the web estate, the fee schedule or the public register, would not have been detected; since a live designation must by law carry a cost-recovery fee and a public register, this residual risk is low.

notes: South Cambridgeshire has no selective or additional HMO licensing scheme; it confirmed in a freedom of information response that no selective licences have ever been granted. Mandatory HMO licensing costs £895 for up to five bedrooms, plus £36 per extra room.
research: The best-evidenced negative in the batch, because the council has answered the question directly in writing. FOI DISCLOSURE, DIRECT PRIMARY ADMISSION: the council publishes its own FOI responses. 'Request 8596 Selective Licensing Scheme Property Licenses' asks 'regarding your Selective Licensing Scheme (if you have one in place)' and South Cambridgeshire's own responses are: '1. What was the estimated number of properties that were thought to require a Selective License from the outset? - None'; '2. How many licenses have been granted? - None'; '3. How many properties are the Council aware of, that are unlicensed and require a license - None'. 'Request 8597 Civil Penalties for Selective Licensing Scheme' similarly answers 'How many Civil Penalty Notices were issued relating to privately rented properties in years 2018 and 2019? - None' and '- Not applicable'. SITEMAP SWEEP: 757 URLs, independently reproduced, ZERO containing 'selective'. FEE TEST: mandatory only, quoted verbatim from the current schedule, verified by direct fetch: 'HMO Licence Fees 2026/2027 - The application fee for a 5-year licence for 2026/2027 is £895 for up to 5 bedrooms, any additional bedrooms are priced at £36 per room. Renewal of the licence is £544 for up to 5 bedrooms, any additional bedrooms are priced at £24 per room.' SECTION INDEX: /housing/renting-privately/ lists nine pages (HMO, poor condition, mobile homes, moving in, landlord legislation, private sector housing guide, Renters' Rights Act, and two council lettings brands). No selective licensing page. The HMO guidance and regulations pages were fetched and grepped: no mention of selective or additional licensing; the only application routes offered are 'Apply for a House in Multiple Occupation Licence' and 'Apply to renew a House in Multiple Occupation Licence'. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) STATUTORY-POWERS BOILERPLATE, which would have caught a careless sweep, because two LIVE pages contain the words 'additional licensing' and 'selectively licence' in close proximity: 'The legislation introduced a new definition of a House in Multiple Occupation and requires mandatory licensing of HMO's with 3 Storeys or more and with 5 or more occupants. This legislation also includes powers to introduce additional licensing ... and also to selectively licence properties', under a heading literally reading 'Housing Act 2004 Part 2 and 3 - Licensing of Houses in Multiple Occupation'. A Part 2-and-3 heading on a live council page is exactly the shape of a true positive. But these describe the POWER in the Act, not its exercise: no designation, area, ward, date or fee accompanies them, and the council's own FOI answer confirms zero licences. (2) s.254 DEFINITION: the guidance page defines an HMO as '3 or more tenants are occupying the property who form 2 or more households'. (3) 'any additional bedrooms are priced at £36 per room', a surcharge on a mandatory licence. (4) The three PDFs matching 'selective licensing' are FOI REQUESTS, and their content is a negative rather than a positive. LIMITATION: the on-site search FAILED its control test (client-side JS rendering, zero result rows even for control queries) and was not relied on. ModernGov also failed its control test, returning chrome only, so committee papers could not be keyword-searched, and democracy.scambs.gov.uk did not resolve. The FOI responses date from around 2020; their currency is carried forward by the 2026/2027 fee schedule and the current sitemap sweep, both consistent with no scheme.

notes: South Derbyshire has no selective or additional HMO licensing scheme. Only mandatory HMO licensing applies, for homes let to 5 or more people from 2 or more households. Licence work is charged at hourly rates, from £42 to £65 an hour depending on the officer.
research: THRESHOLD: the live HMO pages (a three-chapter article reached by crawling the live private-landlords page) state 'from 1 October 2018 HMOs with five or more occupiers forming two or more households regardless of the number of storeys will be subject to HMO licensing' and list only the three mandatory categories. No selective or additional licensing is mentioned anywhere in the three chapters. FEE TEST, which CORRECTS an initial finding that South Derbyshire publishes no HMO fee at all. The housing fees and charges page DOES carry a housing-licensing section headed 'Licensing of Houses in Multiple Occupation', covering 'Application for new licence', 'Amendment of licence' and 'Transfer of licence', charged hourly at 'Manager £65 / hour, EHO £54 / hour, Assistant £42 / hour'. So the mandatory regime is fee-bearing, which makes the fee test properly discriminating here: there is a mandatory HMO licensing fee line and NO selective and NO s.56 additional licensing fee line. The separate Licensing fees and charges page was read in full and covers only private hire, food export certificates, animal licences, gambling and scrap metal dealers. SITEMAP SWEEP: 748 URLs, independently reproduced, ZERO containing 'selective'. IMPORTANT CAVEAT ON THAT SWEEP: the sitemap is STALE, every loc using the retired south-derbys.gov.uk domain and omitting the live HMO page entirely, so it was NOT treated as sufficient on its own and was supplemented with a live crawl and an archive sweep. ARCHIVE SWEEP: Wayback CDX queried for BOTH southderbyshire.gov.uk and the legacy south-derbys.gov.uk domain across their full recorded history: ZERO archived URLs matching 'selective'. CONSULTATIONS: the licensing policy-consultations page carries only a 'Draft Animal Welfare Licensing Policy 2026-2031'. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) NEIGHBOUR BLEED, DERBY CITY, actively checked and clean. Derby City Council has operated selective licensing and South Derbyshire wraps around it, so a Derby scheme description on a South Derbyshire page would be easy to misattribute. All three South Derbyshire private-rented-sector pages were grepped for 'derby city' and 'selective': ZERO hits. (2) VOLUNTARY ACCREDITATION: the landlord support page describes accreditation requiring landlords to 'abide by the EMLAS Code of Management, prove they are fit and proper ... and have at least applied for any licences that they should hold by law'. The East Midlands Landlord Accreditation Scheme is voluntary, and the phrase 'any licences that they should hold by law' does not create a designation. (3) s.254 DEFINITION: chapter 1 opens 'A house or a flat in which three or more people forming two or more households share some basic facilities'; chapter 2 then correctly sets the licensing trigger at five. (4) 'additional benefits in tenant support services' on the landlord page, an unrelated sense. LIMITATION: this is the weakest-sourced negative of the twelve, though still adequately sourced. The on-site search FAILED its control test (returning HTTP 411 or client-side-only results, with zero result rows for control queries) and was not relied on. The CMIS committee system is ASP.NET postback-driven and could not be keyword-searched, and southderbyshire.moderngov.co.uk returned HTTP 522; committee papers were therefore not reachable. The sitemap is stale as noted. The finding rests on the live HMO pages, the hourly-rate housing fee schedule, the dual-domain archive sweep and the consultations page.
